meta: You download an open model and the file is 16 GB, and your laptop runs out of memory? Bit explains quantization: rounding the numbers so the model gets about four times lighter.

muc.title: The model is too big
muc.text: Mark tries downloading an open model, like in video 114, but the file is 16 GB and his laptop runs out of memory.

muc.title: Rounding the numbers
muc.text: Bit explains: a model is billions of numbers. Quantization rounds those numbers so they take less space. Storing each number in 4 bits instead of 16 makes the model about four times lighter.

muc.title: Like compressing a photo
muc.text: It's like compressing a photo when you send it in a chat: the file gets much smaller, but it looks almost the same.

muc.title: A little less accuracy
muc.text: In return, the model loses a bit of accuracy. 4 bits usually still works well, but squeeze it too hard and the answers get much worse.

muc.title: Reading the file names
muc.text: When you download a model, you'll see labels like Q4 or Q8. That's the number of bits after compression: the smaller the number, the lighter the file.

muc.title: Compare two versions
muc.text: Go to an open model's page, compare the size of the Q4 and Q8 versions, and see which one fits your computer's RAM.
